evidence.supportingExcerpt: Immunity and capacity also limit what a lot can do. In a phase 1/2 study in seven people with severe haemophilia B, an AAV2 factor IX vector infused through the hepatic artery reached therapeutic levels at the highest dose but expression lasted about 8 weeks; the authors' further studies suggested that cell-mediated immunity against capsid antigens destroyed transduced hepatocytes (Manno and colleagues). Neutralising antibodies against the capsid are why re-dosing is hard: a review notes that systemic AAV dosing needs patient stratification by antibody level and that re-administration then becomes very difficult (Naso and colleagues), and a 2024 mouse study, which opens by noting that AAV typically induces long-lasting neutralising antibodies that prevent re-administration, found that transient B-cell depletion (anti-CD20 with anti-BAFF) before hepatic AAV8 delivery allowed effective re-administration (Rana and colleagues). evidence.supportingExcerpt: Three design labels are easy to confuse. Replication-defective means the delivered particle lacks the machinery to propagate as an ordinary virus, which does not replace testing: FDA guidance sets out testing of retroviral vector products, lentiviral ones included, for replication-competent virus during manufacture and in patient follow-up. Self-inactivating means regulatory sequences in the long terminal repeats are disabled: in the original design a 133 base-pair deletion in the U3 region of the 3' repeat was copied to the 5' repeat after reverse transcription and integration, and the vector still expressed from an internal promoter in rat brain and eye (Miyoshi and colleagues). It does not mean the cassette cannot integrate. Integration-deficient means integrase is mutated: with a class 1 integrase mutation, residual integration was lower than with intact integrase by a factor of 500 to 1,250, expression was transient in dividing cell lines and long-lived in non-dividing neural cultures and in mouse brain, consistent with an episomal genome (Philippe and colleagues). The name does not promise zero integration or lasting expression in dividing cells such as T cells.

In clinical use, third-generation self-inactivating vectors disrupt the promoter and enhancer activity of the long terminal repeat, non-integrating vectors lacking integrase have been investigated to avoid insertional mutagenesis, and recombination during manufacture could in theory produce replication-competent retrovirus or lentivirus, which is why lots are tested (Milone and O'Doherty, review).

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A lipid nanoparticle is a formulated fat-based carrier that protects RNA and helps it enter cells. Getting into a cell, releasing usable RNA into the cell fluid and making protein are separate steps, and a particle can succeed at the first without the others.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Read a construct from its 5-prime end to its 3-prime end: cap, untranslated region, initiation context, protein-coding region, untranslated region and poly(A) tail have different jobs. A target list does not specify the finished RNA. Changing a UTR changes a regulatory sequence; changing an amino-acid spacer changes the combined protein. Start-codon context was tested by single-base substitutions around the AUG initiator in a cloned preproinsulin gene, where the best sequence identified changed proinsulin yield over a 20-fold range (Kozak). The interaction of the cap and the poly(A) tail was tested with luciferase mRNAs delivered by electroporation into tobacco protoplasts, Chinese hamster ovary cells and yeast, where the tail's effect depended on the cap (Gallie). A textbook describes the 5' cap, 5' and 3' untranslated regions that regulate translation initiation and mRNA stability, a poly-A tail of about 200 A residues added by poly-A polymerase to cellular mRNA, and a ribosome that moves from the cap to the AUG, with Kozak's rules describing the sequence around it (OpenStax Biology 2e). The cellular tail length is not a rule for engineered constructs: one dendritic-cell study found that a 120-nucleotide tail, an unmasked tail end and two 3' untranslated regions each improved stability and translation, and it measured transcript amount by RT-PCR, protein by eGFP, peptide-MHC density and T-cell stimulation separately (Holtkamp and colleagues), so a doubled reporter signal after a 3' change is one measurement, not a different antigen or a clinical benefit. These are tested constructs and cell systems, not one best sequence for a clinical product.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A computational study of spacer design for class-I-restricted string-of-beads polypeptides reported a fivefold increase in predicted epitope recovery and a 44 per cent reduction in predicted neo-epitope immunogenicity compared with designs without spacers (Schubert and Kohlbacher); these are predictions, not measured protection. Combining an N-terminal leader peptide with an MHC class I trafficking signal at the C terminus improved presentation of class I and class II epitopes in human and mouse dendritic cells and expanded antigen-specific CD8 and CD4 T cells in vitro and in mice (Kreiter and colleagues). In a first-in-human RNA poly-neo-epitope melanoma study all patients developed T-cell responses against multiple vaccine neo-epitopes (Sahin and colleagues; abstract only), and each patient's vaccine in the Rojas pancreatic cancer trial used two uridine mRNA strands, each encoding up to 10 neoepitopes. Mass spectrometry can identify recovered HLA-bound peptides. Caron and colleagues' 2015 review describes class I peptides predominantly 9 to 12 amino acids long and reports that about 10 per cent of acquired spectra could be confidently assigned at a 1 per cent false discovery rate in the workflows discussed. It also describes evidence that mass spectrometry underestimates the self-HLA peptide repertoire, so non-detection does not prove absence. Prediction is not presentation: of more than 1,300 amino acid changes in two mouse tumour models about 13 per cent were predicted to bind MHC class I and a small fraction of those were confirmed by mass spectrometry (Yadav and colleagues). Because a single amino acid after an epitope changed its immunogenicity in a multiepitope DNA vaccine (Livingston and colleagues, already linked), a changed spacer is a changed construct that needs renewed processing and display evidence, while earlier evidence is retained for the parts that did not change.

It also describes evidence that mass spectrometry underestimates the self-HLA peptide repertoire, so non-detection does not prove absence. Prediction is not presentation: of more than 1,300 amino acid changes in two mouse tumour models about 13 per cent were predicted to bind MHC class I and a small fraction of those were confirmed by mass spectrometry (Yadav and colleagues). Because a single amino acid after an epitope changed its immunogenicity in a multiepitope DNA vaccine (Livingston and colleagues, already linked), a changed spacer is a changed construct that needs renewed processing and display evidence, while earlier evidence is retained for the parts that did not change.
